# Background processing across replicas

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `aspnet-background-jobs` · **ASP.NET Core & API Engineering** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S02-Q017](#S02-Q017)

<p>How would you expose a long-running API operation without making the caller wait for processing to finish?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Give long-running work an explicit execution owner and recovery contract across process and replica failures.</p>

<ul>
<li>Separate accepting work from completing it and expose caller-visible status.</li>
<li>Compare execution lifecycle, triggering and durable ownership.</li>
<li>Specify recurring-work timing, overlap and missed-run policies.</li>
<li>Trace retries, cancellation, shutdown and competing replicas to a business invariant.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Request pipeline, middleware and filters](aspnet-request-pipeline.md)

<p>Hosted-service and worker questions establish who runs the work. Submission and recurrence questions define how work starts and how a caller observes it. Failure questions test interruption and repetition; offloading trade-offs check whether changing the request path is justified. Multi-replica scheduling brings these decisions together: a job can outlive a process, so its identity and recovery policy must not remain implicit.</p>

### S02-Q020 · Mechanism

<p>How would you compare IHostedService, BackgroundService, a scheduler and an external queue-based worker for one workload?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q020](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q020)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q020](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q020)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare `IHostedService`, `BackgroundService`, scheduled jobs and external queue-based workers.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>These choices describe overlapping lifecycle, triggering and deployment responsibilities. Explain those axes before choosing rather than treating the names as mutually exclusive products.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Compare background execution choices by lifecycle and failure boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify .NET version, scheduler or broker and deployment topology; consult official lifecycle and delivery documentation before asserting guarantees.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Separate how work is triggered from where it runs and who owns it.</li>
<li>Compare restart behavior, scaling and operational evidence for the workload.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Listing feature names without distinguishing process lifetime from durable work ownership.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Can a hosted service consume an external queue in your design?</li>
<li>Which requirement would make an independently deployed worker worthwhile?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q017"></a>

### S02-Q017 · Application

<p>How would you expose a long-running API operation without making the caller wait for processing to finish?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q017](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q017)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q017](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q017)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you design a long-running API operation so the caller does not wait for processing to complete?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Design the caller-facing submission and observation contract. Separate accepting work from completing work, and clarify what a client can safely conclude from each response.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design an asynchronous operation contract with observable progress and failure.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State completion time, durability requirements and client capabilities; no particular worker or status-code default is assumed.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Define submission, operation identity and status/error transitions.</li>
<li>Trace lost responses and worker failure to a client-visible outcome.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Returning immediately without defining whether the work survives a process restart.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How should a client recover after losing the submission response?</li>
<li>How would cancellation differ before and after processing starts?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q021"></a>

### S02-Q021 · Application

<p>How would you schedule recurring work with an explicit policy for missed runs and overlapping executions?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q021](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q021)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q021](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q021)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you schedule recurring work?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Define what recurrence means for the business and how time maps to work identity. Discuss a schedule as an operational contract rather than only a timer expression.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Translate recurring-work requirements into a testable schedule policy.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State timezone, workload duration, deployment and scheduler/version; confirm time and persistence guarantees in official documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Specify timing, overlap and missed-run behavior with examples.</li>
<li>Explain how to observe successful, delayed and skipped work.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Providing a cron expression without defining downtime or overlap behavior.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What happens if one run lasts longer than the interval?</li>
<li>How would you test a timezone or daylight-saving transition where applicable?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q022"></a>

### S02-Q022 · Failure cases

<p>How would a background worker handle retries, cancellation, graceful shutdown and possible duplicate execution?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q022](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q022)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q022](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q022)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you handle retries, cancellation, graceful shutdown and duplicate execution?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace one job through interruptions and state changes. Graceful shutdown means a controlled attempt to stop; clarify the recovery boundary if that attempt cannot finish.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Protect a job invariant under interrupted and repeated execution.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the worker, .NET version and persistence mechanism; verify documented cancellation and shutdown guarantees rather than assuming completion.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Distinguish retryable failure, cancellation request and committed work.</li>
<li>Trace an abrupt termination and state how a later worker recovers safely.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming a cancellation signal rolls back completed effects or shutdown always finishes.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What if shutdown occurs after a side effect but before the job is marked complete?</li>
<li>How would you prevent retries from overwhelming a failing dependency?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q019"></a>

### S02-Q019 · Trade-offs

<a id="S05-Q044"></a>

<p>When should resource-intensive or long-running work move out of the synchronous request path into a background job?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q019](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q019) · [S05-Q044](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q044)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q019](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q019)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When should work move from the request path to a background job?

</div>

**[S05-Q044](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q044)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When should resource-intensive work run outside the synchronous request path?

</div>

**Why these source prompts share a canonical question:** Same offload decision; retain resource-intensive work as the concrete context.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Judge the decision using caller needs, resource pressure and failure recovery. Moving work changes its ownership and contract, so identify the operational costs as well as shorter request waiting.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose execution ownership from latency, resource and recovery constraints.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Include CPU-, memory- or I/O-intensive work; state workload, client deadline and required durability. This merges the API and cloud-source offloading questions.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connect an observed or proposed bottleneck to a caller requirement.</li>
<li>Compare synchronous and background execution, including status and capacity evidence.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming background execution removes resource cost or makes every workload faster.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>When would synchronous processing still be the simpler correct choice?</li>
<li>How would you detect a background backlog after offloading?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q023 · Production decision

<a id="S05-Q046"></a>

<p>What changes when multiple application replicas schedule or execute the same scheduled or background work?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q023](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q023) · [S05-Q046](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q046)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q023](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q023)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What changes when multiple application instances run the same scheduler?

</div>

**[S05-Q046](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q046)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you make scheduled/background processing safe across multiple replicas?

</div>

**Why these source prompts share a canonical question:** Same multi-replica scheduler safety question; retain scheduled/background scope.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain how work identity and execution ownership span processes. Cover both who triggers a run and what happens if two replicas still begin the same logical job.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about coordination and safe recovery across scheduler replicas.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Include scheduled and background processing from both sources; state topology, scheduler/version and coordination-store guarantees after checking official documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace competing replicas, lost ownership and a later retry.</li>
<li>Define the business invariant and a multi-replica failure test that checks it.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Relying on a process-local flag or claiming a distributed lock alone makes every side effect exactly once.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What happens if execution continues after its ownership lease expires?</li>
<li>How would you test a replica crash during a scheduled run?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Agent-added production exercise: an API submits a CPU-intensive report, and a recurring task also produces reports; three replicas serve requests. Define submission/status behavior and missed-run/overlap policy. Trace a crash during generation and a deployment shutdown while two replicas compete for the same run. Specify ownership, recoverable state and tests of the business invariant, then choose a hosted, scheduled or queue-based execution model without assuming a product guarantee.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Distinguishes request execution from background work and names the main hosting and scheduling choices.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defines ownership and observable states; defends execution placement; handles interrupted, repeated and concurrent runs with explicit recovery and a validation plan.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A worker diagram or claimed lock is not proof of safe execution. Need state-transition traces, interruption tests, or documentation-backed tests of the selected scheduler/store.</p>
